finding.claim: Broken function-level authorization on POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban: the admin check is wrapped in `except Exception`, which swallows the 403 raised by abort(403), so any authenticated non-admin user can ban any user.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller (non-admin) sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban; g.user is the authenticated principal set by upstream middleware (not in this code).
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (protected state-changing operation; body is currently a stub, so impact here depends on the real implementation).

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST with attacker-controlled uid in the path.
require_admin(g.user) is called; for a non-admin user it executes abort(403).
require_admin: user.get('is_admin') is falsy, so abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException.
except Exception catches the HTTPException (HTTPException subclasses Exception), so the 403 is not propagated.
Only a warning is logged; execution continues.
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally for the non-admin caller.
Returns {ok: true} to the non-admin caller.

finding.guards_checked: Checked: require_admin is the only authorization check in the file; no decorator, before_request hook, or blueprint-level guard is visible. The ban handler's try/except is the defect. unban (lines 24-28) calls require_admin without a try block and correctly aborts with 403 before do_unban, so the bypass is specific to ban. Did not verify whether upstream middleware sets g.user to None for unauthenticated requests; if it does, g.user.get raises AttributeError and the handler 500s without reaching do_ban, so the exploitable precondition is an authenticated non-admin session. CSRF protection for cookie-based sessions is not visible in this code and was not confirmed either way.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is the only check and it raises via abort(403) at line 11. The call at line 17 sits inside try, and `except Exception` at line 18 swallows that HTTPException. Line 19 only logs, and do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs regardless. No decorator, before_request hook, or blueprint guard is visible in admin.py. unban (lines 26-27) has no try block, so its 403 propagates and it is not affected.
verdict.reason: For an authenticated non-admin, require_admin aborts with 403 at admin.py:11, the `except Exception` at admin.py:18 swallows it, and do_ban(uid) still runs at admin.py:20, so the ban is reached. Minor trace imprecision: the is_admin check is on admin.py:10 and the abort on admin.py:11, not line 9 (the def line), but the described behavior is accurate. Anonymous callers are not a path: if g.user is unset or None, the AttributeError at admin.py:19 raises outside the try and returns a 500 before do_ban runs.
